title: VeeRwolf (chipsalliance/VeeRwolf)
_note: chipsalliance/VeeRwolf @ 9a919805 (v0.7.5): the reference SoC around the VeeR cores -- AXI interconnect, AXI-to-Wishbone bridge, Wishbone interconnect, system controller, memory wrapper, UART 16550, SPI, over a VeeR EL2 (the `cpu_el2` configuration). It is a FuseSoC project, so the closure is FuseSoC's: the `generate` step runs test/ext_ip/veerwolf_setup.sh, which sets up the `lint` target (= the full veerwolf_core netlist) into VeeRwolf/build and thereby fetches uart16550 1.5.5-r1, simple_spi 1.6.1, wb_intercon 1.4.1 (+ wb_common, verilog-arbiter, cdc_utils), PULP axi 0.25.0 and common_cells 1.20.0 from fusesoc-cores @ def274ab, and GENERATES the AXI / Wishbone interconnects, the EL2 configuration and the version header.  VeeR EL2 1.4 (882027cc, the commit veerwolf.core pins) is cloned by the harness into veer-el2-vw and seeded into FuseSoC's cache, because the GitHub tarball FuseSoC would fetch carries a symlink Python's tarfile refuses.  Rows are VeeRwolf's own modules, the generated interconnects and the Wishbone-side peripherals (uart16550, simple_spi, wb_intercon, wb_common, verilog-arbiter, cdc_utils); the EL2 core, PULP axi and common_cells are closure-only here (they have families of their own).  The board tops (Nexys / Arty / Basys3 / Agilex: Xilinx and Intel primitives, LiteDRAM) are not part of the lint target and are not swept.  Five modules default their width parameters to 0 ("you must override me"); the bind values are the SoC's own: IW 4 (the LSU master id width the AXI interconnect is generated with), DW 32 (wb_cdc's 32-bit CDC), SIZE / MEM_SIZE 4096 (BOOTROM_SIZE), num_masters 3 (the three AXI masters ifu / lsu / sb).  read_slang needs --unroll-limit raised: dpram64 / wb_mem_wrapper clear their 4096-entry memory in an initial loop and the default 4000-iteration budget stops at 'unroll limit exhausted'.
